title: How Netflix Really Makes Money (The $45 Billion Machine)
description:
Netflix brought in $45.2 billion in 2025 and kept almost $11 billion as net profit. In this file we open the money machine behind Netflix: red envelopes and the end of late fees, the $50 million offer Blockbuster turned down, the 2011 price-rise and Qwikster crisis, the move into its own shows and 130+ new countries in one day, the password-sharing crackdown and ads, the $2.8 billion it earned by walking away from Warner Bros., and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Netflix Q4 2025 and Q3 2026 shareholder letters; Netflix Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (SEC); Netflix newsroom (global launch, January 2016); Fox Business and Business Insider/AOL (company history); Entrepreneur (Marc Randolph on the DVD years); Fortune and Newsweek (Blockbuster offer); AP via Fortune (end of DVD service); Quartz and TIME (2011 price rise and Qwikster); CBS/AP (2016 expansion); Al Jazeera, TechCrunch and CNN/AOL (paid sharing and ads); Wikipedia summary of the Warner Bros. Discovery bidding (timeline); TechSpot.

All figures are from company reports where available and are rounded. The 36% content-cost share and the 'under nine hours' comparison are our own arithmetic from Netflix's reported and guided figures. The late-fee origin story is the version Netflix's founders have told publicly. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
